description.value: An fMRI study investigated attentional bias to smoking-related BEGIN and END stimuli in smokers and non-smokers using identification and distraction tasks.

spans.text: To incorporate BEGIN- and END-smoking-stimuli with short stimulus presentation times in an fMRI study, we modified a paradigm developed by Straube et al. ( 2006 ).

value: we expected an attentional bias (smoking-stimuli minus control-stimuli) for BEGIN-smoking-stimuli.
BEGIN-smoking-stimuli (compared to control-stimuli) are hypothesized to elicit activations in the mesocorticolimbic addiction network.
All hypothesized effects were expected to be addict-specific, i.e., significantly stronger in smokers than in non-smokers.
